Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.
The Team:

Celonis grew up with the private sector: Deutsche Telekom, Mercedes-Benz, Uniper and three quarters of the DAX companies rely on Celonis Process Intelligence. Now we are taking the next big step in Germany: scaling our business with the public sector. To make this happen, Celonis is investing heavily through 2029 in its German public sector business.

Over the past year, we have built our Public Sector team from the ground up. Today, a strong go-to-market core team of Account Executives and Value Engineers is in place, working with federal and state-level institutions.

The Bundeswehr is one of our primary target organizations in the public sector. With our Celonis for Defense & Security initiative, presented at the Munich Security Conference 2026, we offer a sovereign and trusted platform that integrates data across systems and optimizes military processes along the entire value chain. This means higher operational readiness through optimized logistics and faster maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) cycles, greater resilience through end-to-end supply chain transparency, and faster IT modernization by connecting existing systems with modern AI applications. Building on our data analysis solution Metropolis, we also help connect information from a wide range of sources into a comprehensive situational picture, enabling faster and better-informed decisions during the actual mission.

To drive this forward, we are now complementing our existing Public Sector team with a highly specialized Account Executive who brings first-hand experience from inside the organization we serve: the Bundeswehr.

The Role:

This is not a typical Account Executive role. You bring the perspective of someone who knows the Bundeswehr from the inside: how its structures work, how processes in logistics, maintenance or procurement really run, and how decisions are made and budgets are approved. You will use this credibility to build trusted relationships across the Bundeswehr and the defense ecosystem, and to position Celonis as a long-term partner for its digital transformation.

Working closely with our Public Sector AEs, Value Engineers and product experts, you will translate the operational reality of the armed forces into compelling use cases, contribute to the creation of solution blueprints, drive opportunities from first conversation to signed contract, and help shape how Celonis enters and grows in this market.

The Work you'll do:

• Build and own relationships across the Bundeswehr – Army (Heer), Navy (Marine), Air Force (Luftwaffe) and Cyber and Information Domain Service (CIR) – and its ecosystem, e.g. the Federal Ministry of Defence (BMVg), the Federal Office of Bundeswehr Equipment, Information Technology and In-Service Support (BAAINBw) and BWI GmbH.

• Engage with decision-makers from leadership, logistics, procurement, IT and digitalization.

• Translate operational challenges into concrete, AI-enabled use cases with measurable impact, e.g. in logistics and supply, MRO and materiel readiness, supply chain resilience, procurement and IT modernization.

• Bring the voice of the Bundeswehr into Celonis: share insights with our product, marketing and value engineering teams to sharpen our offering.

• Own an individual revenue target and drive complex, long sales cycles to a successful close.

• Navigate defense procurement and tender processes (e.g. VSVgV, framework agreements) together with our partners and internal experts.

• Work closely with partners such as consulting firms, system integrators and defense IT providers.

• Represent Celonis at public sector and defense events and conferences.

The Qualifications you need:

• Several years of professional experience within the Bundeswehr, e.g. as an officer or civilian employee, ideally in a leadership role and/or in logistics, procurement, IT, digitalization, planning or organizational development.

• A solid network within the Bundeswehr and a deep understanding of its organization, decision-making and budget and planning processes (e.g. the procurement process CPM).

• First-hand understanding of the process and data challenges in areas such as logistics, materiel readiness, maintenance or procurement.

• A strong interest in moving into a commercial, customer-facing role. Prior experience in sales, business development or consulting is a plus, but not a must. We will support your onboarding into the sales role.

• Strong affinity for technology, data and AI, and the ability to explain complex topics in a simple and convincing way.

• Degree in Technology & Management, Industrial/Business Engineering, Business Informatics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Economics or a comparable degree program

• Grit, a hands-on mindset, and the drive to build something new.

• Excellent communication and presentation skills in German (native or fluent) and English.

• Familiarity with defense procurement processes is a strong plus.

• Willingness and eligibility to undergo a security clearance (Sicherheitsüberprüfung) if required by our customers.

• Ability to adapt to a fast-moving, high-growth environment and approach challenges with positivity, creative thinking and a growth mindset.

Be Part of Building the Future

Dremio is the unified lakehouse platform for self-service analytics and AI, serving hundreds of global enterprises, including Maersk, Amazon, Regeneron, NetApp, and S&P Global. Customers rely on Dremio for cloud, hybrid, and on-prem lakehouses to power their data mesh, data warehouse migration, data virtualization, and unified data access use cases. Based on open source technologies, including Apache Iceberg and Apache Arrow, Dremio provides an open lakehouse architecture enabling the fastest time to insight and platform flexibility at a fraction of the cost.  Learn more at www.dremio.com.
About the role

Dremio's Query Planner & Reflections (QPR) team owns the SQL planner and optimizer — built on Apache Calcite — and the reflections substitution engine that transparently rewrites queries to hit pre-computed materializations instead of raw source data. As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll set technical direction for this system: driving ambiguous, cross-team initiatives, raising the bar through design and code review, and helping other engineers.

What you'll be doing

• Set architecture and technical direction for the Query Planner and Reflections team spanning next-generation features across OSS, Enterprise, and Cloud editions.

• Own design, implementation, and delivery of complex initiatives that cross team boundaries (Query Execution, Catalog, Datalake).

• Work deeply with Apache Calcite and Apache Iceberg, including driving contributions upstream where it benefits Dremio.

• Diagnose the hardest correctness and performance issues in query planning and reflection matching using query profiles, telemetry, and production data.

• Use AI-assisted development tools for code comprehension, debugging, test generation, documentation, and incident analysis, and apply engineering judgment to validate AI-generated code through review, testing, and benchmarking.

• Design architectures that run correctly across deployment models and public clouds.

• Participate in design and code reviews and set technical standards for the team.

• Partner with Product on multi-quarter roadmap decisions and with Support and field teams on the highest-impact customer issues.

What we're looking for

• B.S./M.S/Equivalent in Computer Science or a related technical field or equivalent experience

• 8-10+ years of experience developing production-level software.

• Fluency in Java/C++ is a plus.

• Deep understanding of query planning and optimization: cost-based optimizers, rule-based rewriting, ideally hands-on with Apache Calcite or a similar framework.

• Strong database fundamentals: SQL, performance, schema design.

• Track record of driving system-level architecture decisions and leading complex, cross-team initiatives.

• Setting technical direction for the team or major component.

• Ability to evaluate tradeoffs and make sound decisions when working with unfamiliar or AI-assisted implementations.

• Ability to navigate ambiguous, cross-org problems independently; strong communication skills.

• Understanding of distributed file systems such as S3, ADLS, or HDFS; AWS, Azure, or GCP experience is a plus.

Bonus points if you have

• Experience with distributed query engines.

• Hands-on experience in query processing or optimization, materialized view matching, distributed systems, concurrency control, code generation, Apache Arrow, caching, or disk spilling.

• Contributions to Apache Calcite, Apache Iceberg, or similar open-source planner projects.

About Codat
Codat is an advisory intelligence solution purpose-built for modern commercial banking. Through rich, specialized data, forward-looking insights, and integrated workflows, Codat empowers banking teams to deepen their relationships, grow their revenue, and simplify their day-to-day work.
Founded in 2017 and backed by JPMorgan, PayPal, Amex, Plaid, and Shopify, Codat has successfully powered over 350,000 connections to business customers’ financial systems — and is trusted by industry leaders to turn scattered information into actionable, strategic advantages in real time, every time.
The Role
Some of the biggest commercial banks in the world already work with us. Their relationship managers want to spend their time with clients, not digging through the books to find out what's changed. We're building the thing that does the digging for them.
It's called the Advisory Intelligence Platform. It puts Codat's client intelligence inside the assistant a banker already uses, starting with Microsoft Copilot. Ask it anything about a client and it answers from that client's actual books. Don't ask, and it tells you anyway when something important changes.
Every one of those answers sits on data. Someone has to get that data in, shape it, define it and serve it, so the number the assistant quotes is the right one. That's you. You write production software, and you care about the data it moves as much as the code that moves it.
This role is for an engineer who's growing fast and wants room to grow faster. You'll ship from your first weeks, own what you build once it's live, and work alongside data and AI engineers who'll push you. Codat is AI-first, not AI bolted onto SaaS, and we work that way ourselves: agents take the repetitive work, engineers take the interesting problems.
 
What You'll Work On
• 
The data behind every answer. Services and pipelines that take raw data from accounting platforms, banks and payment systems and turn it into something a model can trust. When a source sends rubbish, your code notices.
• 
The semantic layer. The definitions the model is allowed to use: what counts as revenue, when a month ends, which currency. Get it right and every answer agrees with every other answer.
• 
The signal layer. Spotting when something changes for a client: a customer paying later, cash running tighter, a supplier quietly becoming critical. You'll help build the detection and make it fast and reliable.
• 
The tools the assistant calls. MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and APIs that serve data to agents. You'll build them, test them and find out how they break before a banker does.
• 
Keeping the numbers honest. Tests, data checks and observability that prove a number is right, and catch it the moment it isn't.
You'll Probably Have
• 
Shipped production software that real people depended on, and written most of it yourself. Services, APIs or data systems with tests, not notebooks or config.
• 
Had data be the hard part. A source that sent duplicates, a schema that changed under you, two teams who meant different things by "customer". You fixed it, and you'd design it differently now.
• 
Good engineering habits in Python, C# or another general-purpose language. Tested, modular code the next person can change without fear.
• 
An eye for SQL. You can read a query and tell whether it's right, whoever or whatever wrote it.
• 
Stayed on the hook for something after it went live. You found out why it broke, fixed the cause, and added what would have caught it sooner.
• 
Some time with CI/CD, Docker and cloud (we're on Azure). You've changed a pipeline, not just pushed to one.
• 
A habit of asking why. If someone asks for a number the data can't support, you say so.
• 
AI as part of how you work, and you can explain and defend what it helped you build.
• 
Momentum. More ownership with each move, new stacks picked up quickly, things built that nobody asked for.
• 
Useful, not essential: fintech, lending or accounting; Spark, Databricks or dbt; anything that puts data in front of an LLM.
Don't tick every box? Apply anyway. We're more interested in what you've built and how fast you're growing than in a perfect match.
 
How We Work
We're a small team with plenty to do. Things move fast: we'd rather ship something useful and improve it than polish it in private. What you build is yours from start to finish.
There's no return-to-office mandate, and you can work hybrid or fully remote. We trust you to be around when the team needs you and to deliver what you said you would. What we don't want is anyone staying online late to prove a point.

About RETR

RETR is a mortgage market intelligence platform. Loan officers use us to find the real estate agents worth building relationships with, mortgage companies use us to recruit top producers, and lenders use us to decide who to lend their money through. More than 55% of the Top 100 mortgage lenders are customers.

We were founded in 2022, we are bootstrapped and profitable, and we have never taken outside money. We grew because loan officers told other loan officers about us. That word of mouth is the whole company in one sentence, and it is why customer outcomes are not a service function here. They are the growth engine.

We are fully remote and we operate on a few principles: lead with value, do the right thing, be generous without keeping score. We hire for honesty, integrity, fairness, accountability, and excellence, and we have very little appetite for process that does not earn its place.

The role

This is one of the first Customer Success Managers at RETR, and you will own a book of our enterprise customers end to end: the relationships, the value they get, the renewal, and the growth.

Our enterprise customers are held today by the founders, sales, support, and enablement, and they are held well. This role exists because the book has outgrown what any of them can carry alongside their own jobs. You get a defined set of accounts and the time to go deep on them: exactly how each one is doing, what it needs next, and where it should be a year from now.

You will report to our VP of Customer Advocacy and work alongside the account executives who own new business and large expansions, and the trainers who run onboarding and group sessions.

What you own

Four things. Everything else you do should move one of them.

A plan for every customer. A short written plan for every account in your book: why they bought, who the people are, what they are trying to accomplish, how they actually use the product, where the risk is, and what happens next. New accounts get one within 30 days. Plans get refreshed before every review and every renewal.

The renewal. You own the path to renewal from the day the account joins your book, not from 30 days out. Risk gets named early, in writing, with a plan against it. Nothing should churn without someone having seen it coming.

Expansion. Growth comes from value: new use cases, new features, new product lines, new teams and branches, and the seats that follow once people see what it is worth. You run the smaller expansions yourself and bring in an account executive on the larger ones. Part of your pay is tied to this, and it should feel like the natural result of doing the rest of the job well.

Advocates. Healthy customers become references, case studies, testimonials, referrals, and beta participants. In an industry this relationship-driven, a customer willing to vouch for us is worth more than most marketing we could buy.

Underneath those four, the work is: knowing how customers use RETR and helping them use it better, building relationships with executive sponsors and daily users alike, reading health from adoption and conversation rather than guessing, and bringing what you hear back into the company so the product and the experience get better.

What this role is not

It is not reactive account management, and it is not a job you win by holding a set number of calls a week. Calls matter, but what matters is what happens on them: the relationship built, the plan moved, the value shown, the joy created.

It is not a support queue. We have a support team and they are good. You are not the escalation path for every ticket in your book.

Because we are still building the Customer Advocacy function, you won't be stepping into a perfectly defined playbook. You'll help create it. We want someone who is energized by that.

How we work

RETR is intentionally lean. Automation before hiring, systems before managers, one to many before one to one. Technology and AI should absorb the work that does not need human judgment, so our people spend their time where people are worth the most: understanding a customer's business, solving a real problem, building a relationship, finding the opportunity nobody else saw.

So we do not want CSMs living in spreadsheets or doing repetitive admin. We want them thinking, and immersed/obsessed with our customers.

We are fully remote and async first. We write things down. We measure what you deliver, and in this role that is the health of your book.

What success looks like

A great CSM here can answer these about any account, at any moment, without opening a file:

• Why did this customer buy RETR?

• How are they using it today, and who actually uses it?

• Are they getting value, and how do we know?

• Who inside the organization cares, and who signs the renewal?

• Where could we create more value for them?

• What could cost us this renewal?

• What happens next, and when?

In your first 30 days you will know your book: the renewals coming, the accounts at risk, and the people who matter in each. By 60 days every account has a plan and you have met the sponsors who count. By 90 days you are running the full scorecard, with your first expansions in motion.

Over a year, the work shows up as deeper adoption, earlier risk detection, stronger retention and expansion, and a list of customers willing to say so publicly. Most of all, our customers should feel that RETR understands their business and is invested in it.

What we're looking for

You are probably a strong fit if you:

• Have 3+ years in customer success, account management, or another customer-facing SaaS role, owning a book with renewal or expansion targets.

• Get genuinely curious about how a customer's business makes money, and can connect our product to the outcomes they care about.

• Are comfortable owning the commercial health of an account, not just the relationship: the renewal, the risk, the growth.

• Spot expansion that comes from real value, without turning every conversation into a pitch.

• Notice problems early and act before anyone asks you to.

• Move fast. Customers hear back from you quickly, and plans turn into action in days, not weeks.

• Build relationships deep enough that customers want to vouch for you.

• Use data, AI, and automation to decide where to focus, and save your own time for the conversations that need a person.

• Communicate clearly with everyone from a daily user to a C-level executive.

• Like building playbooks and doing well when the answer is not written down yet.

• Are motivated by having part of your pay tied to keeping and growing your customers.

• Work well with the account executives, support, and enablement people who share your accounts, and make them better at their jobs. 

• Get real energy out of a customer who is winning, and are not satisfied until they are.

Mortgage experience is a major plus. If you have worked in or sold into mortgage lending, whether at a lender, a broker, a vendor, a title or settlement company, or anywhere else in the ecosystem, say so clearly in your application. Our customers are loan officers, branch managers, and mortgage executives whose income moves with rates. Someone who already understands mortgage origination, recruiting, relationship building, and how a loan officer actually spends their day, starts contributing months earlier and earns credibility in the room on the first call.

It is a strong preference, not a requirement. Adjacent fintech, real estate, or proptech experience counts for a lot too, and we will take how you think and operate over a resume line every time.

Compensation and benefits

Base salary $85,000. On-target earnings $115,000, including $30,000 of variable at 100% of target, paid quarterly. Variable can reach 150% of target for strong performance, which puts total earnings around $130,000. Base is a national figure with no location adjustment.
